arithmetic: Bonds payable, net 101,120,368 (= 97,751,236 principal + 4,005,746 premium - 636,614 issuance costs) + Notes payable 29,425,586 = 130,545,954 consolidated. Notes payable by borrower: University 4,414,235 + 511,351 = 4,925,586; hotel subsidiary as carried = 29,425,586 - 4,925,586 = 24,500,000 (agrees with the 24,500,000 assumed in note 16). The note 9 narrative gives the hotel balances as 21,972,952 + 2,500,000 = 24,472,952, i.e. 27,048 less than carried; 27,048 is the 2024 monthly principal instalment quoted in the same note, so the narrative and the balance sheet differ by one instalment. Consolidated total less hotel notes as carried: 130,545,954 - 24,500,000 = 106,045,954 (this subtotal is NOT printed anywhere in the statements; it is derived). No finance lease liability and no line of credit appear on the balance sheet or in the notes. Whole dollars.
entity_note: The only statements are consolidated (Hampton University, the single-member LLCs HUPCI, Atlantic Real Estate and 27th Street, LLC, and 27th Street Hotel, LLC, 58.7% owned and acquired in June 2024, with a 41.3% noncontrolling interest of 4,335,591). There is NO consolidating schedule and no University-only column, so the University's own statements do not present parent-only debt. The notes identify the borrower only for the hotel notes: 24,500,000 as carried (24,472,952 per note 9 narrative) belongs to 27th Street Hotel, LLC; the senior note (about 22.0 million) is nonrecourse, the junior note (2.5 million) is unsecured. All bonds (101,120,368) and the other two notes (4,925,586) are described as obligations of 'the University'; the notes do not split the bonds between the University and its proton-therapy subsidiary. Rule value uses the consolidated figure because that is the audited reporting entity; University excluding the hotel subsidiary would be 106,045,954 (derived).
differences_from_original: Value unchanged. Two refinements of fact: (1) the first pass called the 27,048 gap between the note 9 narrative balances and the balance sheet unexplained; it equals exactly one 2024 monthly principal instalment on the hotel senior note quoted in note 9. (2) Hotel debt is 24,500,000 as carried on the balance sheet but 24,472,952 per the note 9 narrative; both are reported here.
reader_caveats: No going-concern paragraph. Hotel debt was added by an acquisition in the last month of the fiscal year, so 24.5 million of the total is debt of a majority-owned hotel LLC, of which roughly 22.0 million is nonrecourse to the University; the junior 2.5 million note has no fixed maturity date (due on sale, termination of the management agreement or refinancing of the senior note) but is scheduled in 2029 in the maturities table. New borrowing after year end: five further HBCU Capital Financing advances totalling 13,230,623 through December 23, 2024 (facility maximum 91,500,000). A 4,155,117 multifamily note was paid off by the HBCU Capital Financing Program on June 28, 2024. The auditor reported a material weakness (finding 2024-001: material audit adjustments to investments that did not reconcile to manager/custodian statements) and two significant deficiencies. Investments fell from 366.4 million to 244.9 million in FY2024 and 'appropriation of endowment for expenditure' was 146.3 million (note 13, p.28). Bonds are carried net of issuance costs and including premium; principal outstanding is 97,751,236.

reader_caveats: Counting the fully drawn line, borrowings were 4,750,953. 1,611,786 of the finance-lease liability is current because a balloon payment of about 1.2 million on the turf-field lease fell due in July 2024; note 12 says the lease was modified on September 27, 2024 to pay 500,000 of that balloon and spread the rest over the remaining term. The line of credit matured February 2025 and was extended only to May 29, 2025. Liquidity is tight: all 4,774,316 of cash and certificates of deposit is donor-restricted (unrestricted cash nil), accounts payable and accrued expenses rose from 6,801,121 to 12,079,436, and the College says it advanced about 5.2 million of its own funds on donor-funded construction. Document slips that do not change the debt figures: the cash flow statement is headed 'years ended June 30, 2023 and 2022' over 2024 and 2023 columns; the second table in note 13 labels the 2,500,000 line as 'Capital leases' and the 2,250,953 of loan and leases as 'Debt for operations - unallowable', under a 'Total debt at June 30, 2023' caption; the schedule on p.33 shows total assets 100,159,198 against 100,144,198 on the balance sheet; the auditor's emphasis paragraph refers to 'the University'.
